title: Two distinct geometries
caption: Monza trains the pedal model; Silverstone is excluded from training. The planner can query both maps.

title: Measured AI contribution
caption: Matched ablations give a 3.3 s gain on Monza and 1.8 s on Silverstone; both drivers complete clean laps. Single-condition simulator results.

title: Farther is not automatically better
caption: Historical raw-pedal models never produced a valid lap. The 1,000 m zero-departure run timed out, rather than completing safely.

title: Qualifying-to-simulator distribution shift
caption: The saved data begins at 73 km/h, whereas simulation starts at rest. Brake labels are imbalanced; accuracy requires a baseline.

title: Feature relationships
caption: Pearson correlations use training laps 5/11 only. Correlation is descriptive and is not evidence of causal driving rules.

title: What the Random Forest uses
caption: Curvature 40 m ahead has the largest impurity importance in the saved 500 m model; correlated features can share importance.

title: Offline error versus closed-loop behavior
caption: Predictions on repeatedly inspected lap 14 illustrate errors. These are exploratory validation plots, not a pristine final-test estimate.

title: Several model families
caption: Whole-lap two-fold CV with scaling inside folds. Bars show mean MAE and sample SD; RF and SVR are close with limited data.

title: Where corner speed comes from
caption: The red target is calculated by the hand-written planner. Actual speed follows that envelope; this is not independently learned cornering.

title: Same planner on a new circuit
caption: Silverstone speed targets come from its geometry with unchanged parameters. The Monza-trained model contributes only pedal proposals.

title: A fast lap can be invalid
caption: Actual reconstructed trajectories near the first departure: corrected learned pedals alone run outside the boundaries; the hybrid remains inside.
